Subject: POC trial environment setup: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through your use case today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can lock in a POC that proves the success criteria you outlined.

High-level success criteria (from today)
- Inference latency: median <= 200ms for 1k tokens under peak test traffic
- Cost: target tokens/unit cost <= $0.002 for the evaluation workload
- Functional: accurate entity extraction + reranking within agreed thresholds (will share eval prompts)
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate across 48-hour sustained test window

Recommended evaluation plan (2-week POC)
1) Week 0 (prep): sign MOA, agree test dataset, decide environment (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial)
2) Week 1: integration + smoke tests (sample calls, KV/prefix caching enabled)
3) Week 2: ramped workload, run eval suites, review results + next-step decision

Environment options & typical lead times
- Hosted sandbox (fastest): provisioned within 1 business day; Redwood-managed, tokenized logging, short retention for POC
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity): 1-2 weeks for capacity config; isolated GPU pool, good if you want more deterministic throughput
- VPC trial (private deployment): 4-6 weeks (procurement + networking + KMS) — recommended only if you need data to never touch public infra

Action items we need from Acme to proceed:
- Preferred environment option (hosted recommended to move quickly)
- Test dataset (or a clear subset and sample size) and whether production data will be used
- Security/compliance contacts for a brief questionnaire (we'll loop in Redwood Security)

Attached: redwood-poc-playbook.pdf (step-by-step), poc-moa-draft.docx (MOA to review), soc2_evidence.zip (evidence snapshot)

If you confirm hosted sandbox, we can target a kickoff next week and share API keys + an initial checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great questions — answers inline below.

1) Hosted sandbox & data handling
- Yes: hosted sandbox can be configured to only accept anonymized/test datasets. For the POC we recommend a tokenization/PII-scrubbing step on ingest (we can provide a small script sample).
- Retention: POC logs in hosted sandbox can be set to 30 days by default and are accessible to designated Acme users only. We can shorten retention if you prefer.
- Access controls: RBAC for API keys + optional scoped read-only console access for your reviewers.

2) Security review timing
- Typical security questionnaire turnaround (for SMB/mid-market customers) is 3-7 business days for a standard review. SOC2 snapshot included in soc2_evidence.zip should address most questions.
- Hosted sandbox does not require inbound networking changes and therefore is unlikely to be blocked by the security review; VPC trials are the ones that cause procurement delays.

3) Engineering effort (ballpark)
- Week 0 (setup & integration): ~8-16 engineer hours (one backend engineer + short config with our onboarding engineer)
- Week 1 (smoke + minor fixes): ~8-12 engineer hours during ramp period

Recommended immediate plan
- If speed matters: go hosted sandbox. Target kickoff Monday, 22 Feb 2026.
- MOA: please review poc-moa-draft.docx; if ok, sign and return. Vivek will coordinate API key provisioning once MOA is received.
- Contacts & owners:
  - Acme owner for integration: Alex Johnson (engineering lead)
  - Acme security: Priya Singh (security/compliance)
  - Redwood owners: Marissa Cole (sales, kickoff), Vivek Kulkarni (onboarding), Aditya Rao (SRE for config)

Next steps (please confirm by EOD Fri 13 Feb if possible)
- Acme: confirm hosted sandbox + attach sample anonymized dataset or confirm dataset subset
- Redwood: share onboarding checklist + provisional API keys after MOA

I can also set up a 30-45 minute kickoff to walk engineers through the checklist.
